names.legendary: Perseavus, Lord of Perfect Ripeness

lore.common: Stays rock-hard for six days and becomes soup the moment you buy bread. It thinks this is hilarious.
lore.uncommon: Has a stone so enormous that its flesh has to rent space around it. The stone insists on being called the landlord.
lore.rare: Can turn anything it touches into guacamole. The cutlery drawer has been officially declared a dipping hazard.
lore.epic: Released a green tidal wave of guacamole across an entire food festival. The rescuers brought tortilla chips instead of boats.
lore.legendary: Perseavus rules the five sacred minutes between unripe and rotten. Every chef on earth dreams of meeting it, but its throne is guarded by an army of suspiciously expensive brunches.

names.legendary: Broccolossus, Lord of Green Kingdoms

lore.common: Sits at the edge of the plate like a rejected forest. It claims the broccoli wasn't consulted.
lore.uncommon: Looks so much like a small tree that toy squirrels keep trying to climb it.
lore.rare: Hides in mashed potato and surprises anyone who reaches the last forkful. Its timing is impeccable.
lore.epic: Rose through the school dining hall in a thicket of giant green florets. The children declared a national emergency; the rabbits held a festival.
lore.legendary: In the first garden, Broccolossus shielded every tiny vegetable beneath its vast green crown. It remains majestic, even when served with cheese sauce.

names.legendary: Carrotor, Orange Spear of the Deep Earth

lore.common: Crunches louder than the television. It insists the programme is boring anyway.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks into every snowman's face each winter and demands to be called Sir Nose.
lore.rare: Grants night vision to whoever eats it, but only while they are looking for the last slice of cake.
lore.epic: Pulled itself from the field and dragged an entire regiment of rabbits behind it like a carrot-shaped parade float.
lore.legendary: Carrotor's root pierces the earth from one continent to the next. Its green crown has seen the sun rise in two hemispheres at once, and both farmers claim ownership.

names.legendary: Duchess Cherubelle of the Double Stem

lore.common: Spits its stone into the only clean glass at the picnic. Claims perfect accuracy.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to be eaten without its twin. The twins have hired a lawyer.
lore.rare: Launches cherry pits across three gardens. The gnomes have constructed defensive walls.
lore.epic: Rained red cherries over the summer fair until the entire town looked like it had lost a jam-making competition.
lore.legendary: Cherubelle commands an orchard of cherry twins bound by enchanted stems. Separate one pair and a thousand tiny red rebels arrive demanding reunification.

names.legendary: Cocoboros, Wanderer of the Seven Seas

lore.common: Requires a hammer to open and immediately sprays coconut water on the person holding it.
lore.uncommon: Has three tiny eye marks and the unsettling habit of winking with none of them.
lore.rare: Floats across oceans with an entire island's worth of gossip sealed inside.
lore.epic: Fell from a towering palm and struck the beach hard enough to rearrange every sandcastle into a perfect row of tiny fortresses.
lore.legendary: Cocoboros has crossed the seven seas inside its own unbreakable shell. It carries the map to a hidden island, but the map is written on the inside and nobody can crack it open.

names.legendary: Popcornelius, Lord of the Golden Ear

lore.common: Leaves one kernel in your teeth for longer than most friendships last.
lore.uncommon: Demands butter like a medieval tax collector. Accepts no alternatives.
lore.rare: Hears everything through its ears, so the whole field knows the farmer's secrets by lunchtime.
lore.epic: Built a shifting maze that swallowed the entire autumn festival. The exit was guarded by a very judgemental scarecrow.
lore.legendary: Every harvest moon, Popcornelius commands a golden army to rise from the fields. Their thunderous marching sounds suspiciously like microwave popcorn.

names.legendary: Cucumandra, Chill of the Eternal Noon

lore.common: Makes sandwiches soggy then claims innocence.
lore.uncommon: Pretends to be a courgette whenever the chef approaches with a knife.
lore.rare: Can turn a dragon's fiery breath into chilled cucumber water. The dragon refuses to discuss it.
lore.epic: Grew into an enormous green serpent and rolled through the market, leaving a trail of refreshing salads.
lore.legendary: Stayed cool through the scorching reign of the Sun Tyrant. The tyrant eventually abdicated and asked for two slices to put over his eyes.

names.legendary: Aubergorgon, Queen of the Violet Feast

lore.common: Poses as a shiny ornament until somebody puts it in the oven.
lore.uncommon: Absorbs an entire bottle of olive oil and claims it was thirsty.
lore.rare: Uses its glossy skin to show visitors how they will look after eating too much garlic.
lore.epic: Rose from the vegetable market in a royal purple robe and turned every courgette into an unpaid servant. The tomatoes filed a complaint.
lore.legendary: Aubergorgon rules an enchanted nightshade garden where all fruit shines violet beneath twin moons. No one knows whether the garden grows the queen or the queen grows the garden.

names.legendary: Vinerella, Mother of the Thousand Grapes

lore.common: Rolls under the fridge as soon as someone says five a day. It has a thriving colony down there.
lore.uncommon: Drops one grape from its stalk with every step, leaving a trail only the dog understands.
lore.rare: Grows two fresh grapes whenever one is plucked. Local lunchboxes have become dangerously crowded.
lore.epic: Burst from the harvest wagon in a purple avalanche and rolled through town. Every cobblestone became a tiny grape press.
lore.legendary: Vinerella's oldest vine crosses seven valleys without touching the ground. Every grape carries a different memory, and winemakers spend lifetimes arguing over the flavours.

names.legendary: Lemonarch, Lord of the Bitter Sun

lore.common: Makes everyone pull the exact same face after a bite and insists it is a compliment.
lore.uncommon: Sprays a little zest into every cake mix, then demands credit for the entire cake.
lore.rare: Squirts juice into the eyes of anyone who calls it a small orange.
lore.epic: Sent a wave of sourness through the village pancake festival. Every face puckered at once and the judges could only whistle.
lore.legendary: Lemonarch ripened beneath a sun so fierce that even its light tasted sharp. When an ancient feast grew too sweet for the gods, one drop restored the balance, and every guest remembered the taste forever.

names.legendary: Melonius, the Knock-Knock King

lore.common: Rolls off the fruit stand at the slightest bump, dragging the grapes into the escape.
lore.uncommon: Spits a shower of slippery seeds the moment the knife cuts into it.
lore.rare: Grows a cheeky smiling face on its rind whenever someone considers slicing it.
lore.epic: Rolled through the market square like a giant green bowling ball, scattering stalls and collecting a whole procession of runaway fruit.
lore.legendary: Melonius once learned to answer every knock upon his rind, until the entire orchard began knocking back. Farmers swear the trees still tell jokes to one another at night.

names.legendary: Allium, Emperor of a Thousand Tears

lore.common: Makes the cook cry and then has the nerve to ask what is wrong.
lore.uncommon: Peels away its own layers to avoid chores. There is always another onion underneath.
lore.rare: Can make an entire room weep with one tiny cut. The tissues have formed a union.
lore.epic: Attended a comedy festival and turned every joke into a tragic masterpiece. The audience cried so hard the front row needed boats.
lore.legendary: Allium hid his last golden layer in the eye of an ancient dragon. When the dragon finally blinked, rain fell on a drought-stricken kingdom for seven days.

names.legendary: Emperor Satsumo of the Nine Suns

lore.common: Rolls off the fruit bowl whenever someone starts talking about healthy snacks.
lore.uncommon: Hides stringy white pith beneath its peel like untidy winter underwear.
lore.rare: Fires juice from a single segment at anyone who questions its ripeness.
lore.epic: Unpeeled itself in the town square and sent a spiral of zest through every chimney. The whole city smelled like breakfast for a month.
lore.legendary: Emperor Satsumo carried nine tiny suns beneath his rind. When winter swallowed the kingdom, he split himself into segments and gave one warm dawn to each village.

names.legendary: Palmira, Sentinel of the Last Shore

lore.common: Drops a dry leaf beside the sun lounger just as its owner settles in.
lore.uncommon: Hangs one coconut directly over the picnic blanket and looks innocent.
lore.rare: Fans its broad fronds until a heatwave finally admits defeat.
lore.epic: Turned its coconuts into a thunderous drumline during a tropical storm. The island's crabs have practised the rhythm ever since.
lore.legendary: Palmira stood alone after the great storm swallowed the island's lighthouse. Her crown caught the dawn each morning, guiding ships through the reef until the beacon could be rebuilt.

names.legendary: Duchess Persica of the Golden Stone

lore.common: Wears a coat of fuzz that makes every first bite a little ticklish.
lore.uncommon: Drips juice down the elbow of anyone who claims to be eating neatly.
lore.rare: Ripens precisely during its owner's holiday, then sends a smug postcard from the fruit bowl.
lore.epic: Burst at the village picnic and sent a wave of peach juice across the meadow. Ants immediately launched a very successful ferry service.
lore.legendary: Duchess Persica hid a tiny golden stone beneath her soft skin. When planted in a barren valley, it grew an orchard whose first fruits ripened for those who had none.

names.legendary: Pearival, Keeper of the Last Harvest

lore.common: Stays rock hard all week, then turns soft while nobody is looking.
lore.uncommon: Hides one bruise beneath its prettiest side and acts surprised when discovered.
lore.rare: Makes anything nearby go pear-shaped, including carefully baked birthday cakes.
lore.epic: Fell from the tallest branch and bounced through the entire market, turning every stall into a crooked little house. The mayor declared it an improvement.
lore.legendary: Pearival guarded the final ripe fruit during a famine, dividing its sweet flesh among the hungry. At dawn, the discarded seeds sprouted into the first orchard of a new age.

names.legendary: Capsicia, Empress of the Four Colours

lore.common: Spills an impossible number of seeds from a pepper that appears to contain nothing else.
lore.uncommon: Changes from green to gold to red, then demands a wardrobe allowance.
lore.rare: Can grow new crunchy peppers in every empty lunchbox. The school rabbits have become extraordinarily well fed.
lore.epic: Stuffed itself with enough rice to feed the town, then burst into a confetti storm inside the banquet hall.
lore.legendary: Her enchanted peppers shine red, green, yellow and orange. When the four crowns meet, a harvest begins even in the deepest winter.

names.legendary: Ananas Rex of the Golden Grove

lore.common: Pokes everyone who tries to carry it by its fancy green hairstyle.
lore.uncommon: Sits in the fruit bowl wearing a crown and refuses to speak to the apples.
lore.rare: Makes a single sweet bite tingle so fiercely that the diner starts speaking like a pirate.
lore.epic: Rolled into the royal ballroom and punctured every balloon on the ceiling. The party was renamed the Grand Pineapple Coronation.
lore.legendary: Ananas Rex guarded a hidden tropical grove whose fruit cured the bitterness of feuding rulers. Its golden crown is still passed to whichever guest shares the last slice.

names.legendary: King Tuberus, Father of a Thousand Fries

lore.common: Grows little green eyes in the cupboard and watches who steals the crisps.
lore.uncommon: Turns up at dinner covered in mud, claiming it was invited to the plate.
lore.rare: Sprouts legs overnight and marches itself back into the vegetable patch.
lore.epic: Burst through the pantry door trailing a hundred vines and took over the garden. The neighbours are now growing chips along the fence.
lore.legendary: King Tuberus sprouted eyes on every potato in the royal pantry. When the kingdom's crisps vanished, every spud testified against the culprit: the prince, who had salt on his robes.

names.legendary: Pumpkarn, the Harvest Hollow

lore.common: Rolls off the doorstep and tries to scare the cat. The cat is unimpressed.
lore.uncommon: Grows a grin so crooked that the trick-or-treaters think it is laughing at them.
lore.rare: Sends its vines crawling after anyone who steals sweets from the Halloween bowl.
lore.epic: Summoned a procession of glowing jack-o'-lanterns through town. Every carved face sang the same terribly off-key harvest song.
lore.legendary: Pumpkarn once sheltered an entire village inside his hollow golden shell during the autumn storms. Each Halloween his windows shine across the fields again.

names.legendary: Fragaria, Heart of the Summer Feast

lore.common: Wears hundreds of tiny seeds like freckles and refuses to count them for anyone.
lore.uncommon: Leaps out of the punnet and leaves red kisses on every white shirt at the picnic.
lore.rare: Turns its own shadow into jam, catching unsuspecting ants in a sweet, sticky trap.
lore.epic: Sent a tidal wave of strawberry jam through the county fair, carrying the cream-tea tent triumphantly onto the bandstand.
lore.legendary: Fragaria grew the first sweet red fruit where a summer sunset touched the earth. Each year she hides one perfect berry that tastes like a day worth remembering.

names.legendary: Pomodrake, the Fruit That Fooled Kings

lore.common: Squirts its seeds onto white shirts with unnerving accuracy.
lore.uncommon: Turns bright red whenever anyone compliments its little green crown.
lore.rare: Demands a trial by salad to settle whether it is a fruit or vegetable. The jury is still deliberating.
lore.epic: Burst across the midsummer feast in a magnificent wave of salsa and crowned every guest with tomato sauce.
lore.legendary: Pomodrake once ended a century-long argument between the orchard and vegetable garden by growing a tiny pear from its stem. The gardeners now meet weekly for confused tea.

names.legendary: Arboreon, the Witness of First Spring

lore.common: Drops fresh leaves onto the exact patch someone has just swept.
lore.uncommon: Offers excellent climbing branches and refuses to help anyone back down.
lore.rare: Moves its roots beneath garden paths to draw new secret routes for curious children.
lore.epic: Shook a million conkers from its crown, burying the entire park under a rolling sea of shiny brown ammunition.
lore.legendary: Arboreon remembers the first birdsong ever sung beneath a leaf. Every century a new ring of wood appears around that melody, and animals gather at its roots whenever the seasons lose their way.

names.legendary: Melonara, the Summer Moon

lore.common: Fires its black seeds at everyone sitting within picnic range.
lore.uncommon: Is heavier than it looks and very pleased about it.
lore.rare: Rolls back to the market stall no matter how many times somebody carries it home.
lore.epic: Burst open at the beach and released a red wave of sweet juice. The sandcastle builders spent the afternoon rebuilding their sticky moats.
lore.legendary: Grew as large and round as a summer moon. The town hollowed its rind into a swimming pool and celebrated the harvest under its sweet pink roof.

names.legendary: Pomorath, Elder of the First Orchard

lore.common: Drops apples on anyone reading underneath it. Claims gravity is merely enthusiastic customer service.
lore.uncommon: Attracts wasps, squirrels and one extremely possessive hedgehog. The garden has become a diplomatic minefield.
lore.rare: Can move its ripest fruit to the highest branch just as a ladder arrives. The local apple thieves now use climbing gear.
lore.epic: Woke after a century and marched across the countryside, planting orchards with every step. The farmers praised it until it took the motorway.
lore.legendary: Pomorath's roots drink from the same spring as the first harvest. When famine comes, its branches bloom with enough fruit for a kingdom, though it still drops one on every visiting king.

names.legendary: Apricosol, Keeper of the Amber Dusk

lore.common: A fuzzy orange imp that rolls off the fruit bowl whenever someone calls it a small peach.
lore.uncommon: Guards its stone like a dragon guards treasure. Unfortunately the treasure is another small apricot.
lore.rare: Dries into a tiny wrinkled oracle in sunlight. Its prophecies are always about tomorrow's lunch.
lore.epic: Ripened an entire orchard at once and sent rivers of golden jam through the market. The villagers built toast bridges to cross safely.
lore.legendary: Apricosol holds the last warm colour of every sunset inside its stone. When winter lasts too long, it cracks its heart open and paints spring across the mountains.

names.legendary: Asparax, Lance of the Green Dominion

lore.common: A slender vegetable gremlin that refuses to lie down in the saucepan. Calls it standing tall.
lore.uncommon: Its strange magic makes toilets smell peculiar hours after dinner. Claims this is a respectable battle curse.
lore.rare: Launches itself from the soil like a living spear. Builders have started checking their foundations for asparagus ambushes.
lore.epic: Summoned a forest of giant green spears beneath a royal banquet, lifting the entire castle into the clouds. The king was furious until dessert arrived.
lore.legendary: Asparax commands the first spears of spring. Each year it breaks through frozen earth to challenge winter itself, then insists all defeated enemies be served with butter.

names.legendary: Empress Verdant, Labyrinth of Reeds

lore.common: The whole grove creaks like an argument between a hundred wooden doors.
lore.uncommon: Offers free accommodation to pandas. The checkout time is whenever they stop eating.
lore.rare: Moves its winding paths every sunset. Hikers frequently emerge with different birthdays.
lore.epic: Grew around an invading army in one night. The soldiers came out thirty years later carrying picnic baskets and very strong opinions on tea.
lore.legendary: An ancient living maze whose million stalks whisper one shared secret. Those who reach its heart find a panda sleeping on the throne.

names.legendary: Musa, Mother of the Yellow Moon

lore.common: Drops one enormous leaf onto every visitor, like a very slow green handshake.
lore.uncommon: Offers shade big enough for a picnic, provided nobody minds falling bananas.
lore.rare: Swats fruit thieves with its gigantic leaves and then pretends it was the wind.
lore.epic: Bent under a monster bunch and delivered breakfast to an entire village without anyone climbing a ladder.
lore.legendary: Her ancient leaves sheltered the first rainforest through a thousand storms. Every banana in the world is said to curve toward her throne.

names.legendary: Baoboros, Keeper of a Thousand Rains

lore.common: Looks as if somebody planted a tree upside down and forgot to apologise.
lore.uncommon: Drinks enough rainwater to make nearby clouds suspicious. Never offers to share.
lore.rare: Stores an entire dry season inside its enormous trunk. Elephants queue for its opening hours.
lore.epic: Opened the doors of its hollow trunk during a drought and hosted an entire village, including a very fussy bakery.
lore.legendary: Old as the oldest caravan road, Baoboros remembers every season in its rings. At its command the dry earth blooms for one glorious night.

names.legendary: Basiliskio, Emperor of the Green Sauce

lore.common: Hides in the kitchen window and whispers PIZZA whenever anyone opens the fridge.
lore.uncommon: Turns anything it touches bright green. The blender has started wearing goggles.
lore.rare: Fills an entire street with the scent of fresh pizza. Delivery drivers keep arriving at an empty oven.
lore.epic: Transformed the town square into a giant bowl of pesto. The mayor was elected after surviving the first spaghetti tornado.
lore.legendary: Once challenged an Italian grandmother to a cooking duel and won. She still calls it a lovely herb and refuses to recognise the defeat.

names.legendary: Beetrix, Empress of the Crimson River

lore.common: Leaves purple fingerprints on absolutely everything. Calls them autographs.
lore.uncommon: Hides beneath the soil until someone wears their cleanest shirt to dig it up.
lore.rare: Can turn a white dining room pink with a single sneeze. The decorator has retired.
lore.epic: Rolled through the town in a magnificent purple torrent. The mayor's white suit became a historical artefact.
lore.legendary: Her ruby roots drink the colours from sunset and pour them back into the rivers. Even the swans have learned to enjoy being pink.

names.legendary: Birkhilda, Queen of the White Forest

lore.common: Peels strips off its own trunk and leaves them on your doorstep like a very passive-aggressive letter.
lore.uncommon: Its black stripes migrate around its white bark at night. Botanists blame the zebras.
lore.rare: Sneezes pollen across three villages whenever someone calls its dangling catkins earrings.
lore.epic: Shed a blizzard of silver bark so fierce the entire school copied its homework onto trees. Detention lasted until autumn.
lore.legendary: Her white trunks mark paths through forests that no map remembers. Every winter she invites the snow to stay; every spring she politely evicts it.

names.legendary: Morabella, Queen of the Midnight Harvest

lore.common: Makes you reach through a wall of thorns for one berry. It then drops the berry.
lore.uncommon: Turns the picker's fingers purple. It calls this signing the contract.
lore.rare: Grows across footpaths while nobody watches. Hikers must pay the toll in jam.
lore.epic: Wrapped an entire parked car in brambles overnight. The owner emerged a week later with jam and an unexpected gardening qualification.
lore.legendary: Her thorny palace appears only after the last summer rain. Every berry holds a stolen midnight, and every guest leaves with stained lips.

names.legendary: Bluemora, Mistress of the Indigo Moon

lore.common: Stains pancakes a royal shade of purple, then blames the syrup.
lore.uncommon: Rolls under the fridge where it joins an underground colony of forgotten peas.
lore.rare: Turns the tongue of anyone who steals the last muffin bright blue. The village has abolished detective work.
lore.epic: Burst inside the washing machine and dyed every white shirt in the school blue. The headteacher declared an accidental uniform redesign.
lore.legendary: She plucked a berry from the night sky and made the first blueberry. That is why stars look purple when she gets hungry.

names.legendary: Bokzilla, Emperor of the Hundred Woks

lore.common: Crunches so loudly at dinner that the other vegetables ask it to chew with its mouth closed.
lore.uncommon: Tries to escape the wok by leaping onto the cook's hat. Nobody notices until dessert.
lore.rare: Can jump from one frying pan into another without touching the air. Chefs have started placing bets.
lore.epic: Led a cabbage rebellion through Chinatown's kitchens. The dumplings declared neutrality; the noodles did not.
lore.legendary: Bokzilla once stirred an entire monsoon into a wok and seasoned it with ginger. The resulting soup can only be served in swimming pools.

names.legendary: Branchurion, Guardian of Lost Woods

lore.common: Looks like the perfect stick until the dog finds a much bigger stick and abandons it.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to fit through doorways when a child carries it home. Insists it belongs indoors.
lore.rare: Creeps one inch farther from its trunk every night. The treehouse ladder has given up chasing it.
lore.epic: Fell across two fences during a storm and sprouted into a bridge. The neighbours now share a bench and a very intrusive squirrel.
lore.legendary: Branchurion was cut from the oldest tree but never truly separated. Every forest still bends toward it when a lost traveller needs a way home.

names.legendary: Brusselzor, Emperor of Unwanted Seconds

lore.common: Lives at the edge of the plate and judges children who refuse to eat it. The feeling is mutual.
lore.uncommon: Rolls away from every fork and hides beneath the roast potatoes.
lore.rare: Appears on the plate of whoever says I HATE SPROUTS. Has never failed to find its target.
lore.epic: Summoned every uneaten Christmas sprout into a rolling green army. The dog refused to join, citing professional standards.
lore.legendary: Brusselzor ruled the first winter feast from a throne of gravy. All the other vegetables bowed; the children formed a resistance that continues to this day.

names.legendary: Baron Bramblebeard, Lord of Lost Balls

lore.common: Scratches parked cars and blames a passing squirrel. Nobody believes the squirrel anymore.
lore.uncommon: Lets a gardener trim it into a duck, then changes shape into an insult overnight.
lore.rare: Swallows every football kicked over the fence. Deep inside, the missing balls have formed a parliament.
lore.epic: A single rustle released a thousand branches across the garden party. The guests spent three days finding their own shoes.
lore.legendary: His green labyrinth hides every toy ever lost in a garden. Once a century he returns one, always with the wrong child's name on it.

names.legendary: Manihora, Queen Beneath the Harvest

lore.common: Wears bark so tough that the vegetable peeler has filed a complaint.
lore.uncommon: Burrows into the dirt and pretends to be a stick whenever the farmer arrives.
lore.rare: Refuses to be served without proper preparation, sending undercooked plates back to the kitchen like a furious food critic.
lore.epic: Grew beneath two neighbouring farms and started a border dispute that lasted until harvest. Both farmers now own half a root.
lore.legendary: Manihora fed forgotten cities from roots buried deep beneath the earth. Her harvest never ends, provided the cooks follow her ancient rules and nobody skips the boiling.

names.legendary: Cedrion, Guardian of the Aromatic Ages

lore.common: Smells so much like a freshly sharpened pencil that children keep trying to write with it.
lore.uncommon: Protects woollen jumpers from moths. The moths have accused it of monopolising wardrobes.
lore.rare: Can turn a chest of old clothes into a scented fortress. No moth has breached its walls.
lore.epic: Released a cloud of fragrant resin across the valley and forced every invading moth to retreat. The perfumers called it the best year of business in history.
lore.legendary: Cedrion's roots hold the last breath of every forest ever felled. The oldest temples were built from its branches, and their walls still smell of rain and cedar.

names.legendary: Apior, King of the Thousand Strings

lore.common: Leaves green strings between your teeth like a tiny, edible dental appointment.
lore.uncommon: Crunches loudly enough to interrupt a library meeting. The librarian ate the evidence.
lore.rare: Plucks its own fibres like harp strings, enchanting soups into dancing out of their bowls.
lore.epic: Played a single note on its stalks and sent every salad in the banquet hall marching towards the exits.
lore.legendary: Apior commands an army of immortal green strings. When a giant tried to eat him, it spent seven years flossing and surrendered the vegetable kingdom.

names.legendary: Beta Aurora, Keeper of Rainbow Harvests

lore.common: Shows off rainbow stalks so loudly that the spinach has developed an inferiority complex.
lore.uncommon: Adds a bitter flourish to dinner and acts like the chef's most important ingredient.
lore.rare: Grows a replacement leaf the instant one is harvested, exhausting the gardener by lunchtime.
lore.epic: Painted an entire valley with brilliant red and yellow stalks. Travellers mistook the fields for a sunset that had fallen to earth.
lore.legendary: Beta Aurora gathers colour from the first light of dawn and stores it inside her stems. In winter, hungry villages eat her leaves and see spring in every bite.

names.legendary: Cherubark, Keeper of the Red Harvest

lore.common: Places its ripest cherry one centimetre beyond your fingertips. It enjoys the stretching.
lore.uncommon: Invites birds to feast just before the family arrives with baskets. The birds tip generously.
lore.rare: Hurls pits at anyone climbing its branches without asking. Has impeccable aim and no insurance.
lore.epic: Grew a crown of fruit so wide that the entire town had to hold its cherry festival inside the tree. The pigeons were security.
lore.legendary: Every summer Cherubark bears one ruby cherry that grants a forgotten wish. Every autumn a squirrel eats it before anyone learns which wish came true.

names.legendary: Chilithrax, Dragon of the Thousand Suns

lore.common: Offers itself as a harmless garnish. The first bite reveals its excellent poker face.
lore.uncommon: Hides all its heat in one tiny seed. You will find that exact seed.
lore.rare: Can make a grown chef cry by merely being placed on a chopping board. The onion is furious about the competition.
lore.epic: Turned a five-star kitchen into a volcanic spa with one sneeze. The health inspector gave it a Michelin star and fled.
lore.legendary: Chilithrax is the pepper that taught dragons to breathe fire. Every thousand years one dragon returns asking for a milder version, but he refuses.

names.legendary: Tannenkrampus, King of the Twelfth Night

lore.common: Drops one needle whenever someone says it looks lovely. The carpet is now a forest floor.
lore.uncommon: Makes the cat's favourite bauble roll off its branch every night. A long war has begun.
lore.rare: Rearranges its ornaments while everyone sleeps. The angel on top has begun writing complaints.
lore.epic: Wrapped the entire shopping centre in tinsel and demanded that every store play a different carol at once. The result was classified as psychological warfare.
lore.legendary: Tannenkrampus carries a thousand stolen Christmas wishes in his branches. He grants one each winter, usually to the household pet, who has terrible taste in presents.

names.legendary: Cocotyr, King of the Drifting Isles

lore.common: Leans toward the water as if eavesdropping on the waves. The waves have nothing useful to say.
lore.uncommon: Drops coconuts precisely where sunbathers thought it was safe. The beach towels are nervous.
lore.rare: Walks slowly down the shoreline when no one looks. Has crossed three property boundaries this summer.
lore.epic: Bent in a hurricane and launched a squadron of coconuts over the sea. A neighbouring island sent a formal diplomatic protest.
lore.legendary: Cocotyr's roots grip the oldest island in the ocean. When the tide rose too high, he picked up the island and walked it to safer waters, leaving the maps catastrophically inaccurate.

names.legendary: Vaccinia, the Ruby That Defied Gravity

lore.common: Is so sour that the lemons make a face when it arrives.
lore.uncommon: Bounces out of the fruit bowl and blames the blueberries.
lore.rare: Floats above the bog at night, luring jam makers into a very sticky treasure hunt.
lore.epic: Ricocheted through a holiday dinner, knocking every gravy boat into the mashed potatoes. A family tradition was born.
lore.legendary: The ancient bogs protect Vaccinia, whose crimson berries refuse to sink even in the deepest waters. A king once tried to drown one and lost his crown instead.

names.legendary: Currantia, Queen of the Missing Second

lore.common: Is so tiny it gets mistaken for a crumb. Takes great offence.
lore.uncommon: Falls out of every bun and rolls toward the nearest important document.
lore.rare: Corrects anyone who calls it a raisin, using a surprisingly booming voice.
lore.epic: Escaped from a Christmas cake and bounced through the town clock. All the clocks started arguing about teatime.
lore.legendary: Once slipped between two ticks of the universe's oldest clock. That missing second now belongs to Currantia, who spends it napping every day.

names.legendary: Cypresseon, Keeper of Eternal Horizons

lore.common: Grows straight up while every other tree sprawls and shows off.
lore.uncommon: Stands in a cemetery so solemnly that even the squirrels whisper.
lore.rare: Can hide an entire flock of owls inside its narrow shadow. Nobody understands the geometry.
lore.epic: Raised a wall of living green spires that stopped the winter wind at the village gates. The villagers kept the wall and sold their umbrellas.
lore.legendary: Was planted to remember the name of a forgotten queen. It has watched kingdoms vanish without bending, and its roots still cradle her crown.

names.legendary: Medjoolar, Sweetheart of the Sand Gods

lore.common: Sticks to every finger and expects you to appreciate the affection.
lore.uncommon: Hides its stone just where the unsuspecting bite will land.
lore.rare: Makes plain porridge taste like a royal dessert. The porridge feels underqualified.
lore.epic: Glued an entire caravan's supplies into one enormous sweet. The camels voted to keep it.
lore.legendary: Born from a palm that once shaded a thirsty god, Medjoolar carries the sweetness of lost oases. A single bite is said to reveal the way through any desert.

names.legendary: Mortarbore, Keeper of the Last Forest

lore.common: Creaks in the wind until people start confessing secrets to it.
lore.uncommon: Rents holes in its trunk to owls. The woodpeckers handle maintenance.
lore.rare: Borrows leaves from living trees at night, leaving the forest convinced autumn has started early.
lore.epic: Rose from the forest floor as a towering skeletal guardian. The lumberjacks left their axes and opened a bird sanctuary.
lore.legendary: Long after the ancient forest fell silent, Mortarbore sheltered the last owl, beetle and bat. Its heart is hollow, yet whole generations still find a home inside.

names.legendary: Saint Dillian of the Eternal Pickle

lore.common: Has the posture of a feather duster and the confidence of a royal chef.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks into pickle jars at night to whisper outrageous gossip to the cucumbers.
lore.rare: One sprig can turn a swimming pool into brine. The lifeguard now serves sandwiches.
lore.epic: Seized control of the town bakery and replaced every wedding cake with a seven-tier pickle. The brides are forming a resistance.
lore.legendary: According to ancient jars, Saint Dillian preserved the last cucumber during the Great Famine of Sandwiches. It is still crunchy three thousand years later.

names.legendary: Pitayra, Last Orchard of Dragons

lore.common: Looks like a baby dragon and tastes disappointingly polite.
lore.uncommon: Sneezes black seeds at anyone who doubts its dragon ancestry.
lore.rare: Glows hot pink in the moonlight and hatches a tiny paper dragon every spring.
lore.epic: Burst open at the harvest festival, releasing a cloud of pink-scaled dragonlings. The fruit judge hid under the trophy table.
lore.legendary: The first dragons sealed their summer fire inside Pitayra's scales. On the rare night it blooms, a whole orchard shines like a constellation of sleeping wyrms.

names.legendary: Driftmar, Memory of a Thousand Shores

lore.common: Claims to be a pirate ship. Was formerly a fence post.
lore.uncommon: Washes up in a new country each week and insists it was invited.
lore.rare: Its twists show the shapes of every creature it met at sea. The crabs use it as a family album.
lore.epic: Gathered the timbers of a hundred lost ships and built a floating village in one storm. The inhabitants refuse to return to land.
lore.legendary: Driftmar has touched the coasts of every kingdom that ever fell into the ocean. When held to the ear, its grain tells stories the waves forgot.

names.legendary: Durianox, Emperor of the Unbearable

lore.common: Smells like the inside of a gym bag that learned to sweat.
lore.uncommon: Gets banned from elevators and regards this as aristocratic privilege.
lore.rare: Can clear a hotel lobby with one crack in its spiky shell.
lore.epic: Arrived at a royal tasting and evacuated the palace before the chef had cut the first slice. The king still gave it five stars.
lore.legendary: Durianox's scent once repelled an invading army from the Sapphire Kingdom. The grateful people crowned it king, then relocated their capital upwind.

names.legendary: Edamandra, Empress of a Thousand Pods

lore.common: Shoots one bean across the table every time somebody squeezes it.
lore.uncommon: Hides the best bean inside a pod nobody can open politely.
lore.rare: Can hit a moving target with a soybean from the other end of the restaurant.
lore.epic: Led every pod on the sushi conveyor belt in a synchronized launch. The head chef took cover beneath the soy sauce.
lore.legendary: Edamandra cultivated the first green pod in a garden beneath the eastern moon. Each bean she plants becomes a small guardian that protects the harvest until spring.

names.legendary: Ficus Aurea, Keeper of Secret Flowers

lore.common: Has more tiny seeds than useful conversation topics.
lore.uncommon: Invites a pollinating wasp inside and calls it an extremely exclusive garden party.
lore.rare: Hides its flowers inside its own fruit so well that the bees accuse it of cheating.
lore.epic: Dropped ripe figs across the palace courtyard and glued every royal slipper in place. The queen gave her annual speech barefoot.
lore.legendary: Ficus Aurea guarded the secret of flowers hidden within fruit for a thousand summers. A curious king cut one open and discovered an entire miniature wedding in progress.

names.legendary: Firnhelm, the Winter-Crowned King

lore.common: Drops needles across the living room in places it has never been.
lore.uncommon: Hides pine cones in the branches and pretends they're dragon eggs.
lore.rare: Waits until someone walks underneath before releasing an entire hatful of snow.
lore.epic: Sheltered every deer in the forest during a blizzard. At dawn the herd emerged wearing fir needles like royal uniforms.
lore.legendary: Firnhelm once held a winter so fiercely in its highest branches that spring could not reach the summit. To this day, its crown wears snow even when the valleys bloom.

names.legendary: Oakheart, the Tree That Refused to End

lore.common: Leaves a splinter in every hand and calls it a souvenir.
lore.uncommon: Hisses in the fire because nobody remembered to dry its logs.
lore.rare: Refuses to catch alight until the guests give up and put their coats on. Then it roars triumphantly.
lore.epic: Stacked itself into a wooden giant beside the winter festival and marched through the village leaving warm footprints of glowing embers.
lore.legendary: Oakheart was once the oldest tree in the forest. Even divided into a thousand logs, it remembered the songs of the birds and kept the village warm through forty winters.

names.legendary: Zingoria, the Heart of Winter Tea

lore.common: Looks like a tiny knobbly fist and punches every cup of tea with a sharp spicy zing.
lore.uncommon: Adds a zing to every cup of tea, then insists the teapot thank it.
lore.rare: Makes a whole dinner table sneeze at once without a single grain of pepper.
lore.epic: Spiced a batch of gingerbread so fiercely that the biscuits ran across the kitchen shouting about their freedom.
lore.legendary: Zingoria's warmth has revived lost travellers in a hundred winters. Her greatest deed was convincing a frozen dragon to thaw itself for a cup of tea.

names.legendary: Gingerius, the Thousand-Handed Root

lore.common: Reaches out of the vegetable drawer with five crooked little fingers. Nobody remembers buying a hand.
lore.uncommon: Resembles a little hand that points accusingly at the person who forgot it in the vegetable drawer.
lore.rare: Grows new knuckles each time it's left in the dark. It now gives excellent handshakes.
lore.epic: Sprouted across the entire kitchen overnight, pushing the cutlery drawer into the garden.
lore.legendary: Gingerius's ancient roots hold up an abandoned temple. Every spring they shift a little, and the statues wake to complain that the floors are moving.

names.legendary: Gussandra, Queen of the Unkissed Pie

lore.common: Wears a fuzzy little coat and tastes like it has been personally offended by sugar.
lore.uncommon: Makes everyone pucker so fiercely that their faces take a minute to recover.
lore.rare: Hides behind the prickliest branch of the bush and challenges pickers to a duel.
lore.epic: Turned the village baking contest into a chorus of sour-faced judges. The winner was awarded a glass of water.
lore.legendary: Gussandra grew the first sweet gooseberry in a thorny, forgotten garden. The jealous berries declared her a traitor and made her queen anyway.

names.legendary: Jackvine, Guardian of the Cloud Larder

lore.common: Snaps in two with a dramatic crack and demands applause from the chopping board.
lore.uncommon: Winds around the garden pole until the gardener needs a map to find the beans.
lore.rare: Grows a climbing vine overnight and sneaks into the kitchen window to steal the salt.
lore.epic: Sprouted a forest of bean stalks during the county fair. The prize pumpkin vanished beneath a green canopy.
lore.legendary: Jackvine's stalk reaches a castle above the clouds, but the giant pays it rent in golden compost. No one may climb without a reservation.

names.legendary: Guavara, Beacon of the Sweet Isles

lore.common: Looks ordinary until sliced open, then proudly shows off its ridiculous pink interior.
lore.uncommon: Hides a hundred hard little seeds in one bite and calls it treasure.
lore.rare: Sends its sweet scent around corners, leading every fruit fly to an empty cupboard.
lore.epic: Perfumed the harbour so strongly that the sailors followed the smell instead of their charts. They discovered an island of fruit trees.
lore.legendary: Guavara ripens once every hundred summers on an unnamed island. Its fragrance guides lost ships safely ashore, where the crew must listen to one extremely long fruit story.

names.legendary: Hedgeskar, Guardian of the Hidden Gate

lore.common: Swallows footballs and refuses to give them back until someone offers a biscuit.
lore.uncommon: Hides nettles in exactly the place a child reaches to retrieve a lost toy.
lore.rare: Grows taller whenever neighbours are about to have a conversation over it. The neighbourhood gossip is in crisis.
lore.epic: Encircled a village overnight with a towering wall of leaves and thorns. Residents discovered that the postman had been sleeping inside it.
lore.legendary: Hedgeskar guards an old gate into the garden of forgotten seasons. On one midsummer night each century, the leaves part for a visitor who remembers to knock.

names.legendary: Herbarion, Gardener of Lost Flavours

lore.common: Leans into the kitchen window whenever the soup needs a little more seasoning.
lore.uncommon: Changes its scent every time someone brushes its leaves, causing the cook to question their own nose.
lore.rare: Switches the labels on mint and parsley overnight. The pasta sauce tastes suspiciously like toothpaste.
lore.epic: Grew across every windowsill on the street in one night. Breakfast smelled so good that everyone woke up early.
lore.legendary: Herbarion knows the first recipe ever cooked beside a fire. Its ancient leaves restore the taste of meals people thought they would never remember again.

names.legendary: Armoracia, Sovereign of the Burning Nose

lore.common: Looks like an innocent pale root until the grater brings out its personality.
lore.uncommon: Hides so deep underground that the gardener has to write it a letter asking it to come up.
lore.rare: One spoonful of its sauce sends a sneeze ricocheting through every room in the house.
lore.epic: Turned a banquet into a synchronised sneezing contest. The royal gravy boat sailed clear across the ballroom.
lore.legendary: Armoracia once exhaled beneath an enchanted valley and scattered a century of fog. The villagers can still smell roast beef whenever the east wind blows.

names.legendary: Jalapeno Diablo, the Smiling Ember

lore.common: Looks like a harmless green pepper until it meets an overconfident tongue.
lore.uncommon: Makes the dinner guests sweat while the cook insists it is barely spicy.
lore.rare: Changes its heat depending on who brags about tolerating chilli. The loudest guest gets the strongest bite.
lore.epic: Fell into a sleepover pizza and turned every child's ears bright red. The room stayed lit after the power went out.
lore.legendary: Diablo grew from a seed planted in a volcano's shadow. Its first pepper warmed a frozen village, and its second made the village ask very politely for milk.

names.legendary: Kaleopatra, Empress of the Green Curl

lore.common: Collects rainwater in every wrinkle of its leaves and splashes anyone who harvests it.
lore.uncommon: Turns a perfectly good fruit smoothie the colour of a swamp.
lore.rare: Transforms itself into crispy chips and demands to be promoted from vegetable to snack.
lore.epic: Clogged every blender in the county at once, forcing the fitness club to serve sandwiches. The members were secretly delighted.
lore.legendary: Kaleopatra survived the coldest winter the royal garden had ever known. Her leaves curled into an emerald crown, and the frost learned to ask permission before visiting.

names.legendary: Kiwizor, the Emerald Heart

lore.common: Looks like a tiny brown potato wearing somebody else's fur coat.
lore.uncommon: Hides its sweetest half from the spoon, then gives itself away by giggling.
lore.rare: Stares back through a hundred black seeds until the eater suddenly loses their appetite.
lore.epic: Convinced the family dog it was a tennis ball, then led a three-day game of fetch through every greengrocer in town.
lore.legendary: Kiwizor was born with an emerald heart and a coat of humble brown fuzz. Anyone who slices it finds the map to a garden that grows impossible fruits, but only once.

names.legendary: Quatopatra, Empress of the Pucker

lore.common: Looks like an orange that forgot to finish growing. It is sensitive about the subject.
lore.uncommon: Hides a sour centre beneath a sweet peel and watches unsuspecting eaters pull faces.
lore.rare: Can turn a whole fruit salad inside out, making every strawberry taste like its bitter little secret.
lore.epic: Rolled through the royal banquet disguised as an innocent sweet. By dessert the entire court was puckering so hard they could not pronounce the king's name.
lore.legendary: Quatopatra grew in the orchard of a forgotten sun goddess, where sweetness lived in the rind and sourness in the heart. One bite still awakens an ancient song of two opposite seasons.

names.legendary: Alliumax, the Giant of the Welsh Hills

lore.common: Keeps a secret supply of garden grit between its green layers, especially for soup.
lore.uncommon: Pretends to be an onion whenever someone mentions chopping vegetables.
lore.rare: Grows an inch taller every time the neighbour's prize leek is measured.
lore.epic: Became so enormous that the village used it as a jousting lance at the harvest festival. The potatoes acted as judges.
lore.legendary: Alliumax rose from the soil on a misty morning and stood taller than the hills. It sheltered an entire village beneath its green leaves through a winter storm, and the soup lasted till spring.

names.legendary: Citronella, Tree of the Second Spring

lore.common: Snags sleeves with its thorns and gives them back smelling faintly of lemon.
lore.uncommon: Covers the garden in sweet flowers, then surprises everyone with a crop of sour fruit.
lore.rare: Drops a perfectly ripe lemon into any nearby glass of water, without missing a single straw.
lore.epic: Showered a heat-struck village with so many lemons that the fountain ran lemonade and the frogs refused to drink anything else.
lore.legendary: Citronella grew from the first lemon planted in a forgotten desert oasis. Beneath its flowering branches, travellers found sweet shade and clear water; each spring it returns a little of that miracle.

names.legendary: Elder Stumpstead, the Winter Inn

lore.common: Offers free rooms to beetles and charges them one crumb of bark a night.
lore.uncommon: Sends a log rolling at anyone who tries to borrow firewood without asking.
lore.rare: Opens a hidden mossy door to reveal a kingdom of sleepy toads with tiny crowns.
lore.epic: When the villagers dismantled it for winter, a thousand creatures marched out carrying protest signs made of leaves. The villagers built them a better hotel.
lore.legendary: Elder Stumpstead has sheltered the forest's smallest creatures through a hundred deep freezes. It is said even the last surviving firefly keeps a room there, waiting for spring.

names.legendary: Lady Lychara, the Hidden Jewel

lore.common: Wears a prickly pink coat over the slipperiest little belly in the fruit bowl.
lore.uncommon: Rolls out of its shell looking like a pearl that has made several questionable decisions.
lore.rare: Fires its smooth brown stone into the teacup of anyone who complains about peeling fruit.
lore.epic: Disguised an entire banquet's jewellery as peeled lychees. The visiting duke accidentally proposed to the dessert.
lore.legendary: Lady Lychara was mistaken for the moon's missing pearl and carried into the heavens by a silver heron. She returned at dawn with starlight trapped in her seed.

names.legendary: Mangora, the Sunseed Sovereign

lore.common: Drips sticky orange juice all the way from your hand to your elbow.
lore.uncommon: Pretends to be ripe until someone cuts it open, then reveals an attitude of solid stone.
lore.rare: Folds its scored flesh outward like a little green-and-gold hedgehog and sneaks off the cutting board.
lore.epic: Unleashed a syrupy flood at the summer market, gluing every flip-flop to the pavement. The fruit sellers escaped on banana skins.
lore.legendary: Mangora grew around a seed warmed by the first tropical sunrise. Its golden flesh can restore one lost summer to a village swallowed by winter.

names.legendary: Aceron, the Tree of Seven Harvests

lore.common: Drops spinning seed wings onto the heads of walkers and calls it an aerial parade.
lore.uncommon: Leaves sweet sap on every parked car, ensuring nobody forgets which tree is in charge.
lore.rare: Sings through its branches when the first sugar-sap begins to rise, waking the hibernating bears.
lore.epic: Shook its red canopy over the valley and turned the entire harvest fair into a blizzard of crimson seed-helicopters.
lore.legendary: Aceron grew seven rings during one impossible spring and fed a winter-starved village from its golden sap. The stump of its first branch is still warm at dawn.

names.legendary: Mentha, Queen of the Garden Gate

lore.common: Plants itself beside one herb and has occupied the entire flowerbed by Thursday.
lore.uncommon: Hides inside lemonade and delivers a surprisingly smug breath of summer.
lore.rare: Erases garlic breath from across the dinner table. The restaurant's garlic bread has started filing complaints.
lore.epic: Crawled beneath the garden fences and claimed every vegetable plot in the village. The gardeners now negotiate border treaties over mint tea.
lore.legendary: Mentha sent roots beneath the old city until mint sprang from every crack in its streets. On midsummer nights the cobblestones breathe cool air and whisper her name.

names.legendary: Nectariel, the Summer Without Fur

lore.common: Looks like a peach that forgot its furry coat and would rather not discuss it.
lore.uncommon: Rolls into the fruit bowl and makes every peach feel scandalously overdressed.
lore.rare: Bruises at the faintest insult, then turns the bruise into a little purple face.
lore.epic: Turned the market stall into a polished dance floor with its smooth skin. The peaches slid off in spectacular confusion.
lore.legendary: Nectariel held the last warmth of summer inside its glowing skin. Each autumn its juice rekindles the orchard's colours for one final golden afternoon.

names.legendary: Quercurion, Elder of the Rootbound Court

lore.common: Drops acorns onto the shed roof with the precision of an angry percussionist.
lore.uncommon: Rents its branches to squirrels and charges exactly one forgotten nut per season.
lore.rare: Knows where every acorn was buried, even the ones the squirrels forgot. It has become their most annoying librarian.
lore.epic: Showered the royal garden with a thousand acorns during the autumn feast. The guards slipped, the squirrels cheered and the king declared the tree a public nuisance.
lore.legendary: Quercurion stood through the rise and fall of kingdoms, sheltering countless generations beneath its crown. Deep in its roots it guards the first acorn ever planted in the valley.

names.legendary: Lady Okramucus of the Unstirred Pot

lore.common: Gets chopped into little green wheels and leaves the knife feeling suspiciously sticky.
lore.uncommon: Wears fine fuzz like a velvet coat and insists the cook address it as Your Squishiness.
lore.rare: Thickens soup so quickly that the ladle needs permission to leave.
lore.epic: Conquered the annual gumbo cook-off by turning every competing stew into a single enormous jelly. The judges ate their way out with teaspoons.
lore.legendary: Lady Okramucus once bound a broken riverbank with a thousand slippery pods. The flood stopped, but migrating fish now have to ask her politely for passage.

names.legendary: Count Oliviero of the Unbroken Branch

lore.common: Pretends to be a grape and leaves the first unsuspecting snacker profoundly betrayed.
lore.uncommon: Rolls away from the cheese board carrying a small ocean of brine.
lore.rare: Spits its stone with sniper precision whenever someone says there are no surprises in a salad.
lore.epic: Hijacked an entire cocktail party by replacing the ice cubes with olives. Every drink now arrived with a tiny, judgmental stare.
lore.legendary: Count Oliviero grew from the olive carried by the first dove of peace. To this day, feuding kings must share his brine before negotiating, and nobody enjoys the first sip.

names.legendary: Olivandra of the Thousand Harvests

lore.common: Stands crooked in the sun as though it has heard a very long joke.
lore.uncommon: Turns the undersides of its leaves silver whenever it wants attention from the breeze.
lore.rare: Its roots locate forgotten wells, then refuse to share their coordinates with anyone carrying a shovel.
lore.epic: Shook a century of olives down at once. The village woke to a green hailstorm and a breakfast that lasted three weeks.
lore.legendary: Olivandra stood at the crossroads before roads had names. Generations of travellers carved promises into her trunk, and she still keeps every one beneath her bark.

names.legendary: Lady Naranja of the Golden Groves

lore.common: Scatters fragrant petals on the washing and calls it a free perfume service.
lore.uncommon: Grows one perfect orange just out of everyone's reach, then watches the ladder arrive.
lore.rare: Drops fruit into the hands of travellers who have forgotten their lunch. Squirrels receive the bruised ones.
lore.epic: Shook its branches at the annual harvest and launched a thousand oranges over the orchard wall. The village football team has never had so many balls.
lore.legendary: Lady Naranja guarded a valley where the sun rarely rose. Each spring her blossoms lit the hills like lanterns, guiding migrating birds back to the same homes.

names.legendary: Papayara, Mother of the Black Pearls

lore.common: Rattles a belly full of black seeds whenever anyone calls it a melon.
lore.uncommon: Turns a brilliant sunset orange on the inside while keeping an extremely suspicious face outside.
lore.rare: Makes tough meat so tender it falls apart on the grill before anyone can say barbecue.
lore.epic: Split open at the summer market and unleashed a thousand bouncing seeds. By evening, the entire town was playing tropical pinball.
lore.legendary: Papayara guarded a black pearl in each of her seeds, gifts to the birds that carried her across distant seas. Every new grove grew where a traveller finally rested.

names.legendary: Petrosia, Queen of the Forgotten Plate

lore.common: Sits untouched beside the potatoes and calls it a hunger strike.
lore.uncommon: Lodges between two front teeth just before the family photograph.
lore.rare: Makes a plain bowl of soup taste like a royal feast, then steals all the praise.
lore.epic: Led every garnish in the palace kitchen in a rebellion against being left on the plate. By dessert, even the butter had joined the picket line.
lore.legendary: Petrosia saved a famine-struck kingdom by teaching its cooks how to make a feast of humble garden herbs. Her crown was woven from the parsley nobody had wanted.

names.legendary: Parsnivar, Herald of the Sweet Frost

lore.common: Looks like a carrot that forgot to put on its bright orange coat.
lore.uncommon: Turns sweeter after the first frost and refuses to admit winter deserves credit.
lore.rare: Sneaks into vegetable soup disguised as a carrot and waits for the surprised faces.
lore.epic: Released a cloud of sweet roasting steam across the entire winter market. Every snowman abandoned its carrot nose for a parsnip.
lore.legendary: Parsnivar grew beneath the frozen fields when the village's stores ran empty. His golden roots rose after the thaw, sweet enough to feed every family until the next harvest.

names.legendary: Passiflora, Keeper of the Hidden Sun

lore.common: Looks ancient and wrinkled even when it has just reached its best day.
lore.uncommon: Rattles its dark seeds in a jelly-filled belly like a tropical maraca.
lore.rare: Adds a spark of sunshine to any dessert, including the very serious school rice pudding.
lore.epic: Split across the summer fair and sent a wave of tangy jelly into every lemonade stall. For a week, the town tasted like a beach holiday.
lore.legendary: Passiflora kept the warmth of a vanished island inside her golden pulp. One taste led lost sailors to the distant shore where the island bloomed again.

names.legendary: Princess Pisella of the Forty Mattresses

lore.common: Spits one green pea across the plate and hides the rest in its shell.
lore.uncommon: Rattles around in the vegetable basket like a tiny maraca full of secrets.
lore.rare: Zips itself shut whenever the cook tries to open it. The peas inside are holding a meeting.
lore.epic: Fired a volley of peas across the royal dining hall, turning the banquet into the world's smallest snowball fight. The queen requested another round.
lore.legendary: Princess Pisella hid a magical pea beneath forty royal mattresses to find a true ruler. Only the kindest visitor noticed it and set it back in the garden, where an entire green kingdom grew.

names.legendary: Persimora, Fruit of the Second Autumn

lore.common: Looks deliciously ripe until one bite turns your entire mouth into a desert.
lore.uncommon: Waits on its branch like a glowing orange lantern while the other fruit goes home.
lore.rare: Ripens only when the first frost arrives, sending sweetness through the orchard like a secret signal.
lore.epic: Dropped from every tree at once and bounced down the village lanes. The market had to declare an orange emergency.
lore.legendary: Persimora held a single golden fruit through a winter that lasted seven years. When it finally fell, the snow melted and the sleeping orchard remembered how to blossom.

names.legendary: Pinelord, Witness of the First Snow

lore.common: Drops needles inside your boots and insists it is just sharing its foliage.
lore.uncommon: Glues a passing squirrel to its bark with one blob of sap. The squirrel demands legal advice.
lore.rare: Whispers directions through the wind to travellers lost among identical trees.
lore.epic: Held its green branches high through a blizzard that flattened every other tree. The forest animals opened a warm little market beneath it.
lore.legendary: Pinelord remembers the first snow to touch the mountain and the footsteps of everyone who crossed it. Its oldest needles fall only when an old traveller finds their way home.

names.legendary: Damsonia, Queen of the Second Ripening

lore.common: Looks perfectly ripe until one bite reveals a stone the size of a complaint.
lore.uncommon: Hides behind the leaves until the fruit-picker has given up and gone for tea.
lore.rare: Turns itself into a prune, then back into a plum when no one is watching. The jam maker is losing sleep.
lore.epic: Dropped from the orchard by the thousand, painting every roof purple before the summer parade. The mayor declared it fashionable.
lore.legendary: Damsonia ripened in the middle of winter, so boldly that spring arrived to complain. It lost the argument, and the orchard enjoyed two harvests that year.

names.legendary: Pomeloth, Prince of the Hidden Grove

lore.common: Needs a knife, two thumbs and a long lunch break to get through its peel.
lore.uncommon: Hides a surprisingly delicate fruit behind a wall of thick, bitter rind.
lore.rare: Rolls down a hill, sweeping away market baskets without bruising one sweet segment inside.
lore.epic: Fell from a cart and bowled through an entire fruit fair, scattering the stalls like skittles. The judge gave it first prize anyway.
lore.legendary: Pomeloth sheltered an entire family of field mice inside its enormous rind during a century-old storm. The mice still tell stories of the sweet city beneath the peel.

names.legendary: Prunelda of the Forgotten Orchard

lore.common: Looks like a grape that has received forty years of disappointing news.
lore.uncommon: Hides among the cereal and pretends it has always been there.
lore.rare: Wrinkles anything it touches, including a shiny apple and the cook's new apron.
lore.epic: Drained the moisture from an entire fruit market and declared itself mayor of Dried Town.
lore.legendary: Prunelda grew on the last tree of a desert orchard, surviving a thousand summers without rain. One bite restores a forgotten memory, usually about a very bad haircut.

names.legendary: Quinsera, Keeper of the Golden Preserve

lore.common: Looks like a pear but fights the kitchen knife like a little rock.
lore.uncommon: Perfumes the fruit bowl, then turns everybody's mouth inside out with one bite.
lore.rare: Releases a sweet fragrance that leads lost cooks straight to the pantry.
lore.epic: Turned an entire orchard into fragrant crimson jelly after one autumn rain. The villagers spent a week toast-shopping.
lore.legendary: Quinsera preserved the last golden fruit of a vanished garden in a jar of ruby jelly. Whoever tastes it can smell a loved one's kitchen from any distance.

names.legendary: Raphanora, Crimson Heart of the Garden

lore.common: Bites back with a peppery sting when someone calls it a tiny beetroot.
lore.uncommon: Hides under the soil with its bright red cap sticking out like a cheeky hat.
lore.rare: Grows so quickly that the gardener finds a new radish every time they turn around.
lore.epic: Burrowed under the vegetable competition and burst out as a row of enormous scarlet roots. The judges used a wheelbarrow for the ribbons.
lore.legendary: Raphanora grew a crimson root beneath the king's throne, lifting it through the palace roof. The king now addresses his subjects from the vegetable garden.

names.legendary: Raisendra, Archivist of Old Vines

lore.common: Pretends to be a chocolate chip in a biscuit. Its disguise never improves.
lore.uncommon: Hides at the bottom of the lunchbox and waits until the sandwich is gone.
lore.rare: Can shrink any plump grape into a raisin with a smug little wink.
lore.epic: Led a thousand raisins across the bakery to replace every chocolate chip overnight. The children formed a protest committee.
lore.legendary: Raisendra holds the final sweetness of a sunken vineyard in each wrinkle. Once a year, the vines rise in a fragrant dream and offer their forgotten harvest.

names.legendary: Redovius, Witness of a Thousand Springs

lore.common: Drops a twig from so high up that it takes an entire picnic to reach the ground.
lore.uncommon: Drinks the morning fog before the valley gets any, then apologises by making more shade.
lore.rare: Shelters an entire family of owls in a hollow branch and keeps their secrets for centuries.
lore.epic: Grew beyond the clouds in a single thunderstorm. The climbers found an entire weather system among its highest branches.
lore.legendary: Redovius stands so tall that thunderclouds use its crown as a bench. It has counted a thousand springs and is still waiting for the weather to clear.

names.legendary: Rosmarina, Keeper of Forgotten Names

lore.common: Pricks the cook's finger then insists it is only trying to season the stew.
lore.uncommon: Gives potatoes a glorious aroma and demands a share of the gravy in return.
lore.rare: Remembers where every lost recipe was put. Unfortunately, it also remembers who cheated at the village bake-off.
lore.epic: Sent a single scented gust through the town during the festival. Every resident abandoned their plans and went home for roast dinner.
lore.legendary: Rosmarina's leaves remember every story told beside a hearth. The oldest sprig can recite the names of people whose own descendants have forgotten them.

names.legendary: Verdebell, Empress of the Endless Greens

lore.common: Drops its finest lettuce leaf onto the floor just as the guests sit down.
lore.uncommon: Stirs the dressing only after the last person has decided they did not want any.
lore.rare: Hides all the croutons beneath the cucumber and demands a treasure map before giving them up.
lore.epic: Tossed so violently at a banquet that a cabbage landed on the chandelier. The host declared it the first airborne salad course.
lore.legendary: Verdebell once served a salad so magnificent that the Moon descended to steal a crouton. She charged it extra for dressing, and the tides have been salty ever since.

names.legendary: Shrubmancer, the Hedge That Knows

lore.common: Hides the garden hose and rustles smugly whenever someone searches for it.
lore.uncommon: Grows a suspiciously human-shaped tuft every time the neighbour complains about trimming.
lore.rare: Mimics the exact shape of the gardener who pruned it. The family now has a leafy second grandad.
lore.epic: Grew a living maze around the entire garden centre in one night. Customers followed the exit signs and emerged holding twenty extra plants.
lore.legendary: Shrubmancer remembers every creature that ever rested beneath his branches. At sunset, his leaves form their shapes and tell the garden stories that the stone statues have forgotten.

names.legendary: Spinachius, Champion of the Wilted

lore.common: Shrinks to one sad forkful in the pan after arriving as an entire shopping bag.
lore.uncommon: Sneaks onto the pizza as a single leaf and acts as though it saved dinner.
lore.rare: Gives anyone who eats it enough strength to unscrew every stubborn jar lid in the street.
lore.epic: Fed the school tug-of-war team a bowl of leaves and watched them tow the goalposts, the groundskeeper and the entire pitch across town.
lore.legendary: Spinachius transformed a frail garden snail into an unstoppable champion. The snail now carries the farmer's tractor out of muddy fields.

names.legendary: Alliora, the Spring That Would Not Wait

lore.common: Leaves a little green moustache on everybody who eats noodles with enthusiasm.
lore.uncommon: Regrows from the white end left in a glass of water, and calls itself immortal.
lore.rare: Shoots a fragrant green spear that makes even the toughest ogre cry happy onion tears.
lore.epic: Raised a cavalry of green stalks from the noodle bowls of an entire city. The chefs charged into battle carrying chopsticks.
lore.legendary: Alliora emerged as the first green shoot after the longest winter. Her scent woke the sleeping gardens, and every onion in the world turned toward her.

names.legendary: Germinia, Queen of the Forgotten Jar

lore.common: Peeks out of the sandwich and tries to tickle the eater's nose with its tiny roots.
lore.uncommon: Grows on the windowsill and whispers encouraging things to the neighbouring houseplants.
lore.rare: Sprouts so quickly that it ties every shoelace in the kitchen into a knot of delicate white roots.
lore.epic: Burst from the pantry in a great green surge, carpeting the entire staircase in tiny crunchy shoots. The cat declared it a salad buffet.
lore.legendary: Germinia turned a single forgotten jar into a miniature forest. Travellers now say its transparent walls hold a country where every road grows leaves.

names.legendary: Piceara, the Evergreen Violin

lore.common: Drops sticky sap onto the one tent pitched beneath it and calls this free waterproofing.
lore.uncommon: Wears needles like a prickly green coat and shakes them into everybody's picnic.
lore.rare: Hums when the wind threads its branches, sending whole choirs of woodpeckers into a respectful silence.
lore.epic: Shook an entire winter of snow from its branches onto the visiting ski instructor, then grew a new staircase of limbs for the children to climb.
lore.legendary: Piceara grew for centuries on a cliff above the sea. When her wood became a violin, its first note made every pine in the old forest sway in remembrance.

names.legendary: Carambella, Fruit of Five Horizons

lore.common: Gets sliced into perfect little stars and demands its own birthday candle.
lore.uncommon: Polishes its waxy skin until the kitchen lights look like tiny constellations.
lore.rare: Each slice shines with a different star, guiding lost moths home from the pantry.
lore.epic: Scattered hundreds of glowing star-shaped slices across the dessert table, creating a miniature night sky. The guests ate the Big Dipper first.
lore.legendary: Carambella fell from the heavens as a five-pointed fruit. Sailors who followed its light found an island where every tree grew a different season.

names.legendary: Colocasia, Mother of the Rain Leaves

lore.common: Looks like a coconut that forgot to finish growing up.
lore.uncommon: Wears a huge leaf as an umbrella and refuses to share it with frogs.
lore.rare: Turns a pot of plain mashed roots a brilliant violet and makes every guest insist it must be magic.
lore.epic: Opened elephant-sized leaves across the village square during a tropical downpour, making a green roof over the market stalls.
lore.legendary: Colocasia hid a hungry island's first harvest beneath the earth and taught its people how to turn humble roots into a feast. Her leaves still catch the earliest rain.

names.legendary: Thymoria, the Herb of Borrowed Time

lore.common: Hides its little leaves in the stew and enjoys being mistaken for grass.
lore.uncommon: Clings to the herb stalk so tightly the cook loses half the afternoon stripping it.
lore.rare: Steals a minute from every simmering pot and saves them in a fragrant green pouch.
lore.epic: Seasoned the royal banquet with so much thyme that the guests ate yesterday's dinner tomorrow, and nobody could find Tuesday.
lore.legendary: Thymoria planted the herb at the very first sundial. Each sprig grants one precious hour to those who share a meal with someone they thought they had lost.

names.legendary: Tofurion, the Thousand-Faced Feast

lore.common: Trembles whenever someone approaches with chopsticks.
lore.uncommon: Soaks up the flavour of whatever sits beside it and has developed a very confusing personality.
lore.rare: Mimics any dish's taste and texture so perfectly that the roast chicken has accused it of identity theft.
lore.epic: Absorbed an entire spice market and became a walking feast; every street it crossed smelled like a different cuisine.
lore.legendary: Tofurion was born from the first soybean pressed beneath a moonlit stone. It can become any meal but chooses to feed the hungry in the shape they remember from childhood.

names.legendary: Arboros, the Garden That Learned to Walk

lore.common: Gets trimmed into a duck and immediately grows a moustache.
lore.uncommon: Changes shape whenever the gardener steps indoors. The neighbours prefer its dragon phase.
lore.rare: Switches between a lion, peacock and rabbit at sunrise, complete with convincing animal noises.
lore.epic: Marched an entire palace garden of sculpted beasts through the gates and staged a very polite revolution against hedge shears.
lore.legendary: Arboros is an ancient living maze carved into a hundred animal forms. Every full moon its leafy creatures leave their branches to hunt for the gardener who first imagined them.

names.legendary: Stumpelstiltskin, the Second Beginning

lore.common: Provides a damp seat to every unsuspecting walker and refuses to apologise.
lore.uncommon: Counts its own annual rings and gets offended when children guess too low.
lore.rare: Grows a perfectly placed mushroom just as a tired hiker sits down.
lore.epic: Awakened the old roots beneath a cleared forest and grew an entire mushroom village, complete with a little parliament and even littler arguments.
lore.legendary: Stumpelstiltskin carries the memories of every creature that sheltered beneath the tree it once was. When the forest burned, he gathered its surviving seeds and dreamed an orchard back to life.

names.legendary: Turnipha, the Root That Refused a King

lore.common: Rolls away whenever anyone suggests putting it in soup.
lore.uncommon: Wears its purple crown proudly while hiding most of itself underground.
lore.rare: Turns into a glowing turnip lantern at midnight and leads lost children away from the bog.
lore.epic: Grew so enormous that the harvest festival had to be held on its back. The farmers argued over who got to carve the nose.
lore.legendary: Turnipha sprang from a seed planted by a hungry old woman at the edge of winter. When the village tried to buy her for gold, she grew enough roots to feed everyone instead.

names.legendary: Twigmar, the Smallest Wand of Spring

lore.common: Cracks underfoot just as a child tries to sneak up on a friend.
lore.uncommon: Turns into a sword for every child brave enough to fight a dandelion.
lore.rare: Waves tiny spells into existence, mostly tying shoelaces together and encouraging mushrooms to giggle.
lore.epic: Commanded an army of fallen branches to build a magnificent woodland fort overnight. The squirrels demanded balconies.
lore.legendary: Twigmar broke from the oldest tree when the first spring wind arrived. Though no longer than a finger, it can wake a sleeping forest with one gentle tap upon the earth.

names.legendary: Salixara, the Mother of Silver Rivers

lore.common: Trails its leafy branches across anyone sitting on the riverbank.
lore.uncommon: Dips its leaves into the water and shakes them dry on passing ducks.
lore.rare: Catches lost toys from the current with its long green fingers.
lore.epic: Drew every drifting boat to safety with its sweeping branches during a sudden flood. The rowers thanked it by decorating its crown with lanterns.
lore.legendary: Has listened to the river's stories since the first bridge was built. When the water rose to swallow the village, it bent its mighty branches into a living bridge and held them until dawn.

names.legendary: Yambara, the Buried Banquet

lore.common: Hides under the potato pile and calls its knobbly skin a disguise.
lore.uncommon: Refuses to come out of the soil until the harvest basket has been properly cleaned.
lore.rare: Makes the driest earth fertile wherever its sprawling underground tuber touches.
lore.epic: Duchess Yamzilla grew beneath the entire village market and lifted every stall off the ground in a single enormous harvest. The vegetable sellers demanded an escalator.
lore.legendary: Yambara was buried as the final meal of a hungry winter and refused to be eaten. By spring her roots had filled a hundred fields, and nobody in the valley went hungry again.

names.legendary: Yuzuhana, Perfumer of the Winter Bath

lore.common: Hides its fragrant oil beneath a skin bumpy enough to offend the lemons.
lore.uncommon: Makes the entire kitchen smell wonderful by sneezing once.
lore.rare: Releases a citrus mist that wakes sleeping flowers in the middle of winter.
lore.epic: Emperor Puckerface squeezed one drop into the palace soup. Every royal portrait on the wall puckered its lips, including the horse.
lore.legendary: Yuzuhana warmed a mountain village by floating in its communal winter baths. Her golden fragrance drifted through the snowfall, guiding weary travellers toward the steam and home.
